item.title: Nachi Falls and Kumano Nachi Taisha: Japan's Iconic Waterfall View — Guide
item.description: Nachi Falls, plunging 133 metres in a single unbroken drop, is the tallest waterfall of its kind in Japan and has been worshipped as a deity since before recorded history — the origin of the Kumano Nachi Taisha shrine that stands on the slope above. The classic view, one of Japan’s most reproduced images, sets the vermilion three-storied pagoda of the neighbouring Seiganto-ji temple against the white column of falling water.
